title: Noetherian criterion for pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if there is an integer $b$ such that $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>b$ and every $H^i(K)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

proof.text: Assume $K$ is pseudo-coherent. Unpack [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]: there is a complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules, vanishing in degrees above some integer $b$, and an isomorphism $E^\bullet\simeq K$ in $D(R)$. Thus $H^i(K)\cong H^i(E^\bullet)=0$ for $i>b$.

For any integer $i$, the cycles $Z^i(E^\bullet)=\ker(d^i:E^i\to E^{i+1})$ form a submodule of the finite free module $E^i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] using that $R$ is Noetherian and the standard finite basis generates $E^i$. Choose generators $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ of these cycles. Their images generate the quotient $Z^i(E^\bullet)/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}=H^i(E^\bullet)$: lift any quotient element to a cycle, express that cycle in the $z_j$, and project the expression. Let $\phi:H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(K)$ be the induced $R$-linear isomorphism. For any $x\in H^i(K)$, express $\phi^{-1}(x)$ as a linear combination of the cycle classes; applying $\phi$ expresses $x$ in their images. This proves finite generation in every degree.

source.place: Tag 066E proof, finite cohomology of finite-free complexes

proof.text: Conversely assume the stated upper cohomology bound and finite generation of every $H^i(K)$. For each integer $i$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] with $M=H^i(K)$. Put its term $R^{\oplus n_j}$ in cochain degree $-j$, and put zero terms in positive degrees. Use $d_j$ as the differential from degree $-j$ to $-j+1$ for $j\ge1$ and zero as the degree-zero differential. Exactness gives $d_jd_{j+1}=0$ and $\varepsilon d_1=0$, so the augmentation, with component $\varepsilon$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere, is a cochain map to $H^i(K)[0]$. Its degree-zero cohomology map is the isomorphism $R^{\oplus n_0}/\operatorname{im}d_1\cong H^i(K)$ induced by the surjective $\varepsilon$ with kernel $\operatorname{im}d_1$; exactness gives zero negative cohomology, and the zero positive terms give zero positive cohomology. The augmentation is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Its terms are finite free and it is bounded above by zero, so [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] says that $H^i(K)[0]$ is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 066E proof, first paragraph; Algebra Tag 00LP (2)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-cohomology-implies-pseudocoherent] to $K$. The same integer $b$ gives its bounded-above hypothesis, and Step 3 gives its pseudo-coherent cohomology hypothesis for every integer $i$. Hence $K$ is pseudo-coherent, proving the converse. No lower cohomology bound or Tor-dimension assumption is used. This is the pseudo-coherent clause of Tag 066B used in the proof of Tag 066E.
